inventory.name: border-shape CSS property (initial none, applies to bordered elements, not inherited; strokes a basic shape as the border and clips the interior; border-radius/corner-shape ignored when set)

border-shape value grammar: ED 'none | [ <basic-shape> <geometry-box>? ]{1,2}' vs shipped Chrome 147 two-shape slash form; the full <basic-shape> production applies — circle()/ellipse()/polygon()/inset()/shape() documented from the launch article plus rect()/xywh()/path() as production members flagged for per-function @supports detection

errors.rationale: CSS properties have no exception surface: a declaration that fails to parse is ignored per standard CSS error handling, and neither the css-borders-4 propdef nor the explainer defines any property-specific error behavior (both fetched 2026-08-02). Feature detection via @supports is documented in the examples.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Purely presentational border geometry: no new input, storage, or cross-origin surface. The ChromeStatus API record carries no security/privacy considerations sections for this feature and the explainer raises none (both fetched 2026-08-02).

errors.rationale: Value grammar shares the property's CSS error-handling model: an unsupported shape function or malformed value invalidates the declaration, which is then ignored; no value-specific error surface exists in the propdef (fetched 2026-08-02).

securityPrivacy.rationale: Same rationale as the property: shape values are presentational geometry with no security/privacy surface recorded in the ChromeStatus record or explainer (fetched 2026-08-02).
